bibliographic.title: Model Risk Governance for AI-Based Compliance Systems in Investment Banking
bibliographic.venue: Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
bibliographic.citation_apa: Chawande, P. (2025). Model risk governance for AI-based compliance systems in investment banking. Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation, 6(3), 2027–2035. https://doi.org/10.54660/.IJMRGE.2025.6.3.2027-2035

methodology.technology_context: AI, machine learning, natural language processing, deep learning, robotic process automation applied to compliance, AML, fraud detection, regulatory reporting, and document parsing

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article addresses AI governance, model risk governance, explainability, fairness, accountability, validation, lifecycle management, and compliance in regulated investment banking, which aligns partially with the review's governance and regulated-context dimensions. However, the provided text contains no discussion of conversational systems, chatbots, agents, LLMs, RAG, guardrails, human handoff, contestation, or other conversational governance mechanisms. NLP is mentioned only for parsing regulatory documents, not for conversational interaction.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage scored conversational_ai at 0/3 and the excerpt set does not confirm LLM or conversational scope; full-text verification is needed to rule out later sections on conversational compliance interfaces.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual paper proposing governance structures for AI-based compliance in investment banking. No empirical sample, data collection protocol, or explicit limitations section is visible in the provided excerpts. Strength is regulatory-context clarity; weakness for review purposes is absence of conversational or LLM-specific operational governance detail.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent for model risk governance in banking compliance, but the supplied text offers limited methodological detail and no direct evidence on conversational or LLM governance. Relevance to the review is partial: strong on regulated AI governance, weak on the review's core conversational-LLM focus.

coding.theme: Model risk governance for AI compliance in investment banking
coding.subtheme: Regulatory alignment and validation of non-transparent ML models
rq_alignment: governance and accountability in regulated AI
human oversight themes only indirectly via audit and regulator scrutiny

synthesis.main_claim: AI adoption in investment-banking compliance increases model risk and creates validation, explainability, fairness, and accountability gaps that require enhanced model risk governance aligned with Basel III, Dodd-Frank, and Federal Reserve reporting requirements.
synthesis.contribution: Integrates regulatory compliance, AI governance, and operational risk into feasible tactics covering validation practices, lifecycle management, and documentation for more transparent, auditable, regulation-compatible AI compliance solutions.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on AI/model risk governance in regulated financial services, especially validation, documentation, and regulatory expectations. Do not treat as central evidence for conversational governance or LLM-specific operational controls unless later full-text sections add that scope.

evidence.excerpt: artificial intelligence models tend to have an iterative, non- linear progression

evidence.claim: High-stakes regulatory reporting requires strict model governance
evidence.excerpt: Any model used to generate such reports based on artificial intelligence has to be of utmost governance because data inaccuracy can hugely affect the macroprudential evaluation
